title: Thermal Shutdown FSM
statement: Create a thermal shutdown controller that disables an output when temperature exceeds a threshold and re-enables it only after the temperature drops below a lower hysteresis threshold. The output must not chatter when temperature hovers near the boundary. A synchronous reset should immediately disable the output.
module_signature: module thermal_shutdown_fsm(input clk, input rst, input [7:0] temp, output reg fan_enable);
behavior: fan_enable remains 1 until temp drops below 90.
rst synchronously disables the fan_enable output.
All state updates occur on the rising edge of clk.
rst is active-high and synchronous unless the problem statement explicitly says otherwise.
Use non-blocking assignments in clocked always blocks.
Outputs must never depend on uninitialized x/z state after reset.
When rst is asserted on a rising edge, registered outputs reset to their documented initial values.
constraints: Do not use combinational hysteresis or latches.
hint: Use separate states for enabled and disabled conditions with hysteresis boundaries.
